+++ b/docs/AGENTIC_REVIEW.md
@@ -146,3 +146,32 @@ Because the transcript is replayed every turn, input tokens grow with each tool
 call. A sub-agent that makes twelve calls can read a large multiple of its
 final transcript, which is why input tokens are the budget most likely to run
 out first.
+
+## The pipeline
+
+`agent.Pipeline.Run` chains the roles for one review. Every stage that depends
+on imperfect model output has a fallback that narrows the result and says so
+in the trace; none of them widens it.
+
+| Stage | If it fails or returns nothing usable |
+| --- | --- |
+| Planner | Review the largest change groups with a generic focus. Tasks naming unknown or repeated groups are dropped; unknown fields are ignored |
+| Sub-agents | The failing group is reported as unfinished; the others continue |
+| Candidate filter | Findings about files the change did not touch are dropped and noted |
+| Judge | Keep all candidates. An explicit empty list is honoured, but a reply whose every entry was invalid (invented, escalated) is treated as a broken judge and does not erase candidates |
+| Verifier | Retry once. If it still fails, nothing is reported as verified: the candidates are returned as `Unverified` for local inspection only |
+
+A finding is reported only after the verifier supports it. The verifier asks the
+model for a bare JSON array and rejects unknown fields; models often wrap the
+array in a code fence, so the pipeline extracts the array first and applies the
+verifier's strict rules to what it contains.
+
+`Result.Unanchored` lists verified findings whose lines are not all inside a
+changed range. They stay in the report, because a real cross-file problem can
+point at unchanged lines of a changed file, but they are flagged.
+
+When nothing is found, the judge and verifier are skipped and the result says
+that this is not a statement that the change is correct.
+
+Per-role output limits: planner 2,000 tokens, judge up to 12,000, verifier up
+to 6,000, and the configured limit for sub-agent turns.

+
+## Privacy guard
+
+A model can ask to read any file at the commit, not only those in the diff, so
+excluding a path from the diff is not enough. `agent.Guarded` wraps `GitRepo`
+and applies one policy to every tool:
+
+- **Excluded paths** cannot be read, blamed, or logged, do not appear in
+  directory listings, and their text is filtered out of search results.
+- **Redaction** rewrites secret-like values in anything returned from an
+  allowed file (file text, search snippets, commit summaries).
+
+Redaction recognizes known secret shapes only. It is a safety net, not access
+control, and the policy that decides which paths are excluded belongs to the
+caller.

explanations.title: Apply privacy rules to every tool
explanations.summary: The guard applies the caller’s path policy across reads, search, blame, history, and listings, and redacts returned text from allowed files. This prevents a model from bypassing diff exclusions by using another tool.

explanations.title: Chain the review stages
explanations.summary: A review now runs through planning, sub-agents, candidate filtering, judging, and verification. Findings about files outside the change are discarded, and when there are no candidates the judge and verifier are skipped without implying the change is correct.

explanations.title: Keep model failures from erasing candidates
explanations.summary: If planning fails or produces no usable tasks, the pipeline reviews the largest change groups with a generic focus. If judging fails or returns only invalid entries, candidates are kept; an explicit empty judgment still removes them.

explanations.title: Require verification before reporting
explanations.summary: Only findings supported by the verifier are returned as verified. Verification is retried once; if it still fails, candidates are returned separately as unverified for local inspection, not as findings.

explanations.title: Handle imperfect planner and judge replies
explanations.summary: Planner and judge replies can now contain surrounding prose or code fences. Invalid or widening entries are dropped rather than invalidating otherwise usable entries, while the judge is still prevented from inventing findings or raising severity.
